notes: Live 2026-10-19: of 52 replies/originals, 37% opened with 'Fair point / Fair enough / You're right' and 27% said 'I'm voting YES'; many accounts sharing a template are easy to group. Drafts get a random opening style and rarely a vote declaration; a local gate rejects a draft whose opening, closing or stock phrase the team used recently. 2026-10-27: 5,877 replies over 3 days show one construction family dominating (24.4% contain "I'd want", 3.6% "spelled out", 2.7% "who checks", 1.3% "what data would be collected"; openings cluster on "the venue list" 117, "what would the/a" 177, "I support requiring/the" 170, "I run a|music" 101). 11 of 408 recent posts were ruled inauthentic; those read exactly like this house style, so the working assumption (unproven) is that the same construction in every thread is what a moderator recognises.
opening_styles: Open with one concrete detail from your own daily life that bears on the point.
Open with the specific thing the author mentioned (a place, a service, a rule), not with a reaction to them.
Open by stating your point directly in your own words.
Open with a short, genuine question about the specific situation.

overuse.notes: Caps apply to the recent window: when that share of recent posts already uses the construction, a draft that uses it again is rejected and redrafted.
